newsitem.title: USA: Netscape, Excite launch global guide.
newsitem.headline: Netscape, Excite launch global guide.

text.p: Netscape Communications Corp and Excite Inc said they have agreed for Excite to produce a new navigation service to provide international users with a central Internet guide.

The new service, to be called International Netscale Guide by Excite, will be available in Japan, Germany, France, Britain and Australia from respective Netscape Web sites and from localised Netscape Communicator products.
Under the agreement, Excite will be responsible for programming, production, operations and advertising sales.
The service is due to be launched in Japan and Germany in the September quarter and be available in France, Britain and Australia by the end of the year.
The service will include local news, information and entertainment in localised languages, replacing and enfolding the international version of Netscape's Destinations Page.
Yahoo! Inc earlier this year struck a similar domestic deal with Netscape, Netscape Guide by Yahoo!.
Details of the deal were not disclosed.

The service is the latest in a flurry of announcements in the last month focused on distribution across the major brand names of the Internet, including Netscape and Microsoft Corp as well as search companies Excite, Yahoo!, Infoseek Corp and Lycos Inc.
These include a series of international forays.

Yahoo! started Yahoo! Japan in partnership with financial backer Softbank Corp in the spring of 1996, and has established what it is dubbing "National Yahoos" in Canada, France, Germany, Japan, Britain and Ireland.
Infoseek last week launched five new localised services and now has services in Britain, Germany, Japan, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Brazil, Denmark and Sweden.

Lycos was among the earliest Internet search companies to begin striking international deals and in May formed a joint venture with media company Bertelsmann AG to create Internet navigation sites throughout Europe in addition to their sites in Germany, France and Britain.
Lycos says it is the number one search engine in Europe.
